title: Tidewater API 4.2 Release Notes
key_sentences: Version 4.2 introduces batch uploads, a new rate limit header and several fixes to webhook delivery.
Please read the breaking changes section before upgrading a production system.
Timestamps in all responses are now returned in UTC with an explicit offset.
Send an array of records to the batch endpoint.
The response contains a job identifier and the number of records accepted.
The window length is sixty seconds for all plans.
The following endpoints still work in version 4.2 but return a deprecation warning.
Contact support if any client fails to parse the new timestamp format.

list_items.text: Batch uploads of up to 500 records in a single request
Partial failures are reported per record
Each batch returns a job identifier
Jobs can be polled or followed by webhook
A new header reports the remaining request allowance
Webhook retries now follow an exponential schedule
Webhooks were sometimes delivered twice after a network timeout.
Search results ignored the page size parameter above 100.
The limit is now enforced at 250 results per page.
Exports of empty collections returned an error instead of an empty file.
Pull the new image and restart the service.
Update the client settings shown below.

code:
docker pull registry.tidewater.example/api:4.2.0
docker compose up -d api

client:
  api_version: "4.2"
  timestamps: utc
  retry:
    max_attempts: 5
    backoff: exponential
notes: Software release notes, 2 pages, with three code blocks in Consolas (JSON, shell, YAML). Running header in two parts, footer "Page N of 2". Bullet lists are CSS-drawn, nested to three levels (disc, circle, square). The upgrade steps use CSS decimal markers. Endpoint names in table cells are in the body font, not code. The warning box is body text.
